### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. autoinflammation with arthritis and dyskeratosis  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.730)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:14374)

**Proposed mechanism:** NLRP1 (HGNC:14374) —DISRUPTS→ NLRP3 inflammasome activation (GO:0032670); NLRP3 inflammasome activation (GO:0032670) —LEADS_TO→ Autoinflammation (HP:0012619); NLRP3 inflammasome activation (GO:0032670) —LEADS_TO→ Arthritis (HP:0002715); NLRP3 inflammasome activation (GO:0032670) —LEADS_TO→ Dyskeratosis (HP:0030175). Loss-of-function mutations in NLRP1 disrupt the normal regulation of the NLRP3 inflammasome, leading to its aberrant activation. This uncontrolled inflammasome activation results in the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines, manifesting as autoinflammation, arthritis, and dyskeratosis.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of distinct causal genes for each disease, or evidence that different functional consequences (e.g., gain-of-function vs. loss-of-function) in NLRP1 lead to the distinct disease phenotypes, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: The presence of common variants in NLRP1 with a minor allele frequency > 1% in gnomAD would cast doubt on its role as a causal gene for rare diseases.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism involving NLRP1 and inflammasome activation could lead to the development of targeted therapies for both MONDO:0014089 and autoinflammation with arthritis and dyskeratosis, potentially by modulating inflammasome activity.

#### 2. respiratory papillomatosis, juvenile recurrent, congenital  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.729)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:14374)

**Proposed mechanism:** NLRP1 (HGNC:7773) —DISRUPTS→ NLRP1 inflammasome activation (GO:0032787); NLRP1 inflammasome activation (GO:0032787) —LEADS_TO→ Innate immune response (GO:0045087); Innate immune response (GO:0045087) —LEADS_TO→ Papillomatosis (HP:0000983); Innate immune response (GO:0045087) —LEADS_TO→ Respiratory distress (HP:0012408). Loss-of-function mutations in NLRP1 disrupt its function in inflammasome activation, leading to dysregulation of the innate immune response. This aberrant immune response contributes to the development of papillomatosis and respiratory distress seen in both juvenile recurrent respiratory papillomatosis and MONDO:0014089.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of loss-of-function variants in NLRP1 in individuals with either disease, or identification of distinct pathogenic mechanisms unrelated to inflammasome activation in each disease. _(variant: Any common pathogenic variant (AF > 0.1%) in NLRP1 associated with either disease would falsify a rare variant mechanism.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of NLRP1 in these distinct conditions could lead to novel therapeutic strategies targeting the inflammasome pathway for both diseases, potentially improving patient outcomes and reducing disease burden.
